- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply downward correction by 1–2% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) mid-period, model frequently underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67); increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to align with sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven reversals; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending strongly.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought bias.
- If sentiment is high and price is rising, model often fails to capture full upside; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.
